outcome: No proof, disproof, or settled case of the Goormaghtigh conjecture as stated (x,y>1, m,n>2, (x^m-1)/(x-1)=(y^n-1)/(y-1)) has appeared since 26 January 2024; work in the window is a computational search extension and unrelated/variant equations.
summary: The Goormaghtigh conjecture (only 31 and 8191 have two non-trivial repunit representations in different bases) remains open. Three arXiv items from the window were examined in full: (1) Grantham, 'No new Goormaghtigh primes up to 10^700' (arXiv:2410.03677, also published as INTEGERS 24 (2024) #A98), which extends a computational search — showing no new Goormaghtigh primes exist below 10^700 — but does not prove or disprove the conjecture, and per the deep-dive rules a search-extension on an existence-type question does not count as a change in scope (it narrows where a counterexample could hide, not whether one exists); (2) a 2025 paper on near superperfect numbers and Mertens' theorem (arXiv:2505.08160), which invokes the *existing* 2005 result of Yuan (proving the conjecture's n=3, odd-n case, which predates the window) to derive a *new conditional conjecture* about near superperfect numbers, but supplies no new result on the Goormaghtigh conjecture itself — it is a downstream application, not progress on the stated problem; (3) a October 2025 paper on the 'Ratat-Goormaghtigh equation' (arXiv:2510.11252), which bounds sums of reciprocals of solutions to the single-variable equation (x^m-1)/(x-1)=N, a related but structurally different question (one repunit expression, not an equality of two), and does not address the two-variable equality that defines the stated conjecture — this is a related problem/variant under §3.1, not a case of it. No source mentions AI, machine learning, or any automated theorem-proving system in connection with any of this work; the search methodology in the Grantham paper (compressed PDF content) could not be read past its structure, but no digestion, announcement, or system card anywhere claims AI involvement, and a broader search for 'Goormaghtigh conjecture AI/solved' surfaced only an unrelated AI result on the Erdős unit-distance/discrete-geometry conjecture, confirming no AI connection to this problem. The Wikipedia article itself is unchanged in substance, still citing Yuan (2005) as the strongest partial result. I agree with the triage's 'none' verdict.
competing_reading: One could argue the Grantham computational extension counts as `progress` since it is new work published in the window and appeared in a refereed journal (INTEGERS). But per §3.1's explicit existence/infinitude rule, a record/search extension on a question of the form 'are there any other solutions' does not count as scope-changing progress unless the record itself is the object of the question (it is not here — the conjecture asks about existence of any further solution, not about a stated numerical bound). I classified it as not moving the needle; a reader applying a looser standard might instead record `progress`/`bound` with no AI role, still leaving `ai_role` as `none`.
what_would_settle_it: A proof or disproof of the general Goormaghtigh conjecture (for all m,n>2), or an explicit third solution pair (x,y,m,n), or a digested proof that no such solution exists (e.g. conditional on abc but subsequently made unconditional).
